answer: LoRaWAN gateways hear the same packet from different directions, and an agent proves its place by sending a signed ping that at least three gateways timestamp: the time differences triangulate a position that must match the claimed spot, like a violet signal rising to its zenith above a flat horizon. A single device pretending to be in three cities would need its packets to arrive at gateways it cannot reach, so the geometry exposes the fake.
